assessment.nobel_worthiness: A combined body of work on how technology, task structure and trade shocks reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets. It has changed how economists and policymakers think about inequality, automation and globalisation. It pairs a clear explanatory framework with credible quasi-experimental evidence and has had large effects on research and on society.
assessment.attribution: The task-based and skill-biased technological change line is mainly Katz and Autor. The local labour-market effects of trade exposure are mainly Autor and Hanson, with Dorn as an important co-author. Three names capture the core, but Dorn's omission is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: The work spans more than three decades. The China-shock findings have been widely replicated, debated and refined, and the core results have held up.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a narrower trade-shock prize that includes Dorn
Ongoing debate over the size and persistence of the China-shock effects
The task framework builds on earlier theoretical work by others

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Links optimal tax theory to empirical behavioural responses through the elasticity of taxable income and sufficient-statistics methods. It bridges public finance theory and administrative-data evidence and has strongly influenced tax policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod and Saez are central on taxable-income responses. Chetty is central on sufficient statistics and the empirical turn. Saez also appears in the inequality candidate and Chetty in the mobility candidate, so credit overlaps across ballots. Stantcheva is too early for inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well replicated, with decades of follow-up work across countries.
uncertainties: Overlap with inequality and mobility candidates that share laureates
Whether the prize should centre on tax design or on the empirical methodology
Credit relative to earlier optimal-tax theorists who have already been recognised

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes input misallocation across firms as a quantitatively important source of cross-country income and productivity differences. It brings micro data into growth and development accounting and has changed how researchers measure the sources of income gaps.
assessment.attribution: The Hsieh-Klenow 2009 framework is the clearest core contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson's closely related misallocation work is partly credited through Restuccia, and the list does not contain Rogerson. Naming two laureates is cleaner but leaves some contribution outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of replication and extension. Measurement assumptions are still debated, but the agenda is well established.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the measured gains to measurement error and the assumptions of the model
Restuccia and Rogerson's parallel contributions
Whether the committee sees this as a single discovery or a measurement tool

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rehabilitates monopsony and imperfect competition as a central framework for wage determination. It explains minimum-wage and wage-gap evidence and affects competition and labour-market policy. This is a major and policy-relevant shift in labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Manning's monopsony synthesis is the clearest core. Ashenfelter's contribution is broader, covering empirical labour methods and early monopsony evidence, which makes it less specific to this discovery. Naidu's contribution is more recent and was not selected.
assessment.maturity: The conceptual framework is established. Empirical work on labour-market power, including concentration, is rapidly developing and still being tested.
uncertainties: Whether Ashenfelter's credit fits this discovery or belongs to a broader lifetime-style recognition
How robust recent concentration-based evidence is
Prior recognition of minimum-wage and natural-experiment work (2021 prize)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit experiments gave credible, widely used causal evidence of labour-market discrimination. They changed both research design and legal and policy debate, and they combine a clear discovery with a transferable method.
assessment.attribution: The Bertrand-Mullainathan résumé study is the signature contribution. Others developed audit methods earlier and the field is broad, so a narrow credit risks omitting pioneers outside the list.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of replication and a large literature that has built on it.
uncertainties: Debate over what correspondence studies measure about discrimination mechanisms
Earlier audit-study pioneers who are not on the list
Whether a single-study contribution is enough relative to broader candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shows with micro data that household debt and credit supply expansions drive booms, busts and the severity of recessions. It reshaped macro-financial thinking after the 2008 crisis and is a clear empirical discovery with strong explanatory power.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators of the household-balance-sheet evidence. Campbell's work on household finance is related but distinct.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of follow-up. It is well replicated, though the horizon is shorter than for the older candidates ranked above.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises
Persistence and external validity of the credit-supply channel
Whether the committee prefers a longer track record

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Developed a systematic theory and empirics of how constitutions, electoral rules and political institutions shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It is a foundational base for modern political economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clear joint authors of the synthesis, in their books and papers. Besley's contribution is substantial and related but partly separate. A two-person credit is defensible, though it omits Besley.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of impact. It is highly mature.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize recognised institutions and growth, which may reduce appetite for another institutions-related award
Credit relative to Besley
Identification quality of the cross-country evidence

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine learning methods for causal inference and heterogeneous treatment effects, including double machine learning and causal forests, have become standard tools in empirical economics and across applied science. The methodological impact is large and broad.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across several groups, including Athey and Imbens, Chernozhukov and co-authors, and Wager and Athey. The ballot does not include all contributors, and Imbens is already a laureate, so a three-person split is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The field is still developing, with about a decade of established use. The lasting importance of particular methods is less settled than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Attribution among many contributors
Whether the methods will remain central as the field moves quickly
Substantive empirical discoveries made with them are still limited
